subject.title: [Docs/Question]: Recommended pattern for telemetry-only message lifecycle capture

question: What security boundary and reliability caveats should OpenClaw document for telemetry-only CRM lifecycle capture using message hooks across Telegram and WhatsApp?
rationale: The current docs expose internal hooks, typed plugin hooks, diagnostic events, and WhatsApp raw-content opt-ins, but only maintainers can decide whether docs should recommend a trusted local integration pattern and what guarantees are safe to claim while lifecycle, pre-send, correlation, and WhatsApp contact-policy trackers remain open.

options.title: Document a cautious trusted-local pattern
options.body: Recommend a trusted local plugin or internal hook only for operator-owned CRM capture, call out raw-content and identifier sensitivity, require per-channel smoke proof, and link the open lifecycle-policy trackers for missing guarantees.

options.title: Defer to existing trackers only
options.body: Keep this issue open until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/50126, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/56349, and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/59560 settle their contracts before publishing any pattern guidance.

options.title: Route as support only
options.body: Answer the reporter in support channels without adding docs, accepting that other operators will not have a durable privacy and lifecycle-capture pattern to follow.

recommendation.title: Document a cautious trusted-local pattern
recommendation.body: Recommend a trusted local plugin or internal hook only for operator-owned CRM capture, call out raw-content and identifier sensitivity, require per-channel smoke proof, and link the open lifecycle-policy trackers for missing guarantees.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current routing signal across docs, product/security framing, and the adjacent metadata-only audit proposal.
